messages.subject: Subsetting data in different facets with different scales
parts:
I have a dataframe wich contains 5 columns, and I need to produce a
facetted bar chart which assigns each value of Categ to a different
facet (3 in this example). I am interested in displaying the counts
denoted by val as a stacked bar chart for each of the variables listed
in Var. The problem I am having is that each categ does not contain
the same var or the same number of var and I have tried dropping
factor levels, converting var to character stings etc. but I can't get
geom_bar() to plot only the required var in each facet, all values of
var are plotted in each facet instead!

ID Var Class Val Categ
1 EL M 1 E
2 EL T 37 E
3 SD M 0 E
4 SD T 3 E
17 TRI M 0 E
18 TRI T 1 E
19 SL M 23 S
20 SL T 27 S
25 MSL M 3 S
26 MSL T 1 S

32 SIM T 0 S
33 AS M 6 A

35 ASD M 0 A

37 AI M 0 A
38 AI T 1 A
Can anyone offer any suggestions? Thanks a lot in advance, Phil

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Subsetting data in different facets with different scales
parts:
Hi:

I think this is one of those cases where coord_flip() bites you in the
backside. In your data, Val is nested within Categ.
If you dispense with coord_flip(), you can get the plot you want with
vertical bar charts as follows:

ggplot(tst, aes(x = Var, y = Val, fill = Class)) +
geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
facet_grid(. ~ Categ, scales = 'free_x', space = 'free')

However, you want horizontal bar charts in each facet, and that
becomes a coordination problem between facets and coordinate systems.
To quote Hadley from a post in 2009, "only Cartesian coordinate
systems are currently supported when scales != 'fixed' ". I believe
(but please correct me if I'm wrong) that's still the case - that
appears to be why you get all levels of Var in each facet when
facet_grid() follows coord_flip().

This type of problem has come up several times before in this group -
I was able to scare up several relevant previous posts by searching
the group archives on 'facet_grid coord_flip bar'; this one in
particular was rather interesting:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/583fcfdced24b483/8e729889f97712b3?#8e729889f97712b3

Brian Diggs had the right idea for a general solution (and I hope to
see something like this in ggplot2 soon), but with R packages now
requiring namespaces, it takes a bit more effort to write
special-purpose code that will work at the command line. My Q & D
suggestion at the end of that post still applies, so to that end, try
this:

## Cumulate the frequencies in each Var so that level T of Class will contain
## the total frequency and level M will contain the frequency in that class.
library('plyr')
tst <- ddply(tst, 'Var', mutate, tVal = cumsum(Val))

# Color the total frequency in class T blue and then overlay
# the frequency in class M with orange in a subsequent layer, both
# using geom_segment(). Adjust the size argument to make the bars wider
# or narrower. Putting color inside aes() generates a factor which will
# produce a legend, whose appearance is controlled with
# scale_color_manual().
ggplot() +
geom_segment(data = subset(tst, Class == 'T'),
aes(xend = 0, x = tVal, y = Var, yend = Var, color = 'blue'),
size = 12) +
geom_segment(data = subset(tst, Class == 'M'),
aes(xend = 0, x = tVal, y = Var, yend = Var, color =
'orange'),
size = 12) +
facet_grid(Categ ~ ., scales = 'free_y', space = 'free') +
scale_color_manual('Class',
values = c('blue', 'orange'),
labels = c('T', 'M'))

Until a more robust geom_hbar() function is implemented in ggplot2,
using geom_segment() to generate the bars is a simplistic compromise.
Of course, if you were stacking five or six levels of Class instead of
two, the code would be a lot more tedious...which is why a robust
solution is preferable.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Subsetting data in different facets with different scales
parts:
Hi:

Try this, starting from scratch with tst. You don't have to create new
variables, but I usually do it as a safety device.

library('ggplot2')
library('plyr')
# reorder the levels of Categ
tst$Cat <- factor(tst$Categ, levels = c('E', 'S', 'A'))
# compute the cumulative sum of Val for each Var
tst <- ddply(tst, 'Var', mutate, tVal = cumsum(Val))

# compute the sum of Val, using transform to map the
# sum across levels of Class
tst <- ddply(tst, 'Var', transform, sVal = sum(Val))
# reorder levels of Var by sVal
tst$sVar <- with(tst, reorder(Var, sVal))

# substitute sVar for Var and Cat for Categ

ggplot() +
geom_segment(data = subset(tst, Class == 'T'),
aes(xend = 0, x = tVal, y = sVar, yend = sVar, color = 'blue'),

size = 12) +
geom_segment(data = subset(tst, Class == 'M'),
aes(xend = 0, x = tVal, y = sVar, yend = sVar, color
facet_grid(Cat ~ ., scales = 'free_y', space = 'free') +

scale_color_manual('Class',
values = c('blue', 'orange'),
labels = c('T', 'M'))

HTH,
Dennis
